newsitem.title: USA: Need arbitration in labor talks-American Air chief.
newsitem.headline: Need arbitration in labor talks-American Air chief.

text.p: American Airlines Chairman Robert Crandall said Thursday that arbitration may be needed to avert a strike threatened by the airline's pilots.
"I think mandatory binding arbitration should be required" to prevent airline strikes, he told a House Transportation subcommittee.
Asked if he thought an arbitrator should step in to the current talks between union pilots and his company, Crandall replied, "Yes, I do."

The pilots have said they would like to resolve their dispute with American, the nation's second-largest carrier, without arbitration. They plan to strike after midnight on Friday if no agreement is reached, a move that would disrupt plans for hundreds of thousands of travelers.
Arbitration would mark a new phase in the negotiations. The two sides have already been in mediation under the guidance of the National Mediation Board since Monday.
